name: B10-0252/2026 (Renew) – Situation of women and girls in Afghanistan following the Taliban’s adoption of the Criminal Procedure Code for Courts
title: JOINT MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the situation of women and girls in Afghanistan following the Taliban’s adoption of the Criminal Procedure Code for Courts
part_text:
The European Parliament condemns the Taliban's new Criminal Procedure Code for Courts, saying it deepens the oppression of women and girls. The text is an opinion, not a law. It criticises the European Commission for inviting Taliban representatives to Brussels and asks European Union countries not to recognise the Taliban, not to send Afghan women back, and to give them protection. It also supports international efforts to hold Taliban leaders accountable.

- The code is condemned, but the Parliament cannot change it; it only states its position.
- Afghan women and girls are most affected, along with the European Commission's talks with the Taliban.
- Next, the resolution goes to the Council, the Commission and member states; no binding action follows.
